issues.title: Method brace on same line
issues.description: The rule requires opening braces to appear on a new line after method declarations, but this method has its opening brace on the same line as the declaration (K&R style).
issues.rule_name: Opening Braces Must Be on New Line (Allman Style)

issues.title: BackgroundQueueSize incorrectly rejects zero value despite 'non-negative' contract
issues.description: The BackgroundQueueSize property validation was changed to reject values less than or equal to zero, but the error message states 'must be non-negative' which includes zero. According to the XML documentation, null represents no limit. While zero is semantically different from null, the validation is now inconsistent with the documented contract that explicitly states 'non-negative' (which mathematically includes zero). This prevents callers from setting a zero queue size if that was their intent, even though zero is a valid non-negative integer. The validation logic contradicts the error message, creating a confusing API contract.

issues.title: RetainedFileCountLimit allows zero value violating positive-only constraint
issues.description: The RetainedFileCountLimit property validation was changed from rejecting values <= 0 to only rejecting values < 0, which now allows zero as a valid value. However, both the XML documentation and the error message explicitly state that this must be a 'positive' value, and zero is not positive. The remarks indicate this controls maximum retained file count - a value of zero would mean no log files are retained, which could lead to complete log loss. This violates the documented API contract and creates a dangerous configuration scenario where all logs could be immediately discarded.

issues.title: Premature null assignment in TryGetValidatableTypeInfo violates out parameter semantics
issues.description: The validatableTypeInfo out parameter is now being set to null at the beginning of the method before iterating through resolvers, rather than after the loop when no resolver was found. While this may appear equivalent, it violates proper out parameter semantics and the contract implied by [NotNullWhen(true)]. If a resolver incorrectly returns true while leaving the out parameter unassigned or null (a buggy resolver implementation), the early null assignment would mask this contract violation. Additionally, this creates unnecessary assignment overhead since the parameter will be overwritten by successful resolvers. The original pattern of assigning null only when no resolver succeeds is more semantically correct and provides better detection of misbehaving resolvers.

issues.title: Empty <returns> XML documentation on public method
issues.description: The public API method `AddAzureWebAppDiagnostics` includes a `<returns>` XML doc tag with no content. This results in incomplete XML documentation for a public API, violating the requirement that public APIs have complete XML documentation (including meaningful `<returns>` content when applicable).
issues.rule_name: Public APIs Must Have XML Documentation Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64092 - Doc updates

structured_output.summary:
This PR is described and titled as a documentation update for APIs published under .NET monikers. Most of the 13 touched files are XML doc-comment edits: summaries rewritten to "Gets or sets..." / "Represents..." style, defaults moved into `<value>` blocks, behavior descriptions moved into `<remarks>`, and `<see langword>` used for null/true/false. Those edits are mostly accurate and consistent with the .NET doc conventions.

However, the PR also contains three runtime changes that are not documentation: `AzureFileLoggerOptions.RetainedFileCountLimit` now accepts 0 (`value <= 0` became `value < 0`), `BatchingLoggerOptions.BackgroundQueueSize` now rejects 0 (`value < 0` became `value <= 0`), and `ValidationOptions` reorders an out-parameter assignment and changes a method's brace style. The first of these contradicts the new docs in the same PR ("strictly positive") and silently disables log file pruning when 0 is set, so it should not merge as written.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The doc-only intent is sound, but the RetainedFileCountLimit threshold change is a real regression risk: the new docs say "strictly positive," the error message still says "must be positive," and a 0 value now turns off retained-file cleanup in FileLoggerProvider, so old log files accumulate. The BackgroundQueueSize change is a behavior change that the error message ("must be non-negative") does not describe. Both threshold edits look like accidental operator changes in a doc PR and need to be reverted or explicitly justified and tested.

architecture.overview:
The affected code is the Azure App Service logging stack in src/Logging.AzureAppServices. `AzureFileLoggerOptions` and `AzureBlobLoggerOptions` extend `BatchingLoggerOptions`. Their property setters validate values, and the values are consumed when the logger provider is constructed. `FileLoggerProvider` uses `RetainedFileCountLimit` to decide how many daily log files to keep, and `BatchingLoggerProvider` uses `BackgroundQueueSize` to bound the BlockingCollection that feeds the background writer. The Validation and Caching.SqlServer options classes are documentation-only in this PR, apart from a small reordering in `ValidationOptions`.

The PR changes what the public XML docs promise, and it also changes two setter thresholds. The docs for those two properties now describe a strictly positive value, but the setter for RetainedFileCountLimit accepts 0. That means the documented contract and the enforced contract disagree after this change.
steps: Entry point: users configure `AzureFileLoggerOptions` or `BatchingLoggerOptions` through the options pattern. Each property setter validates its input and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for out-of-range values.

The setter for `RetainedFileCountLimit` in AzureFileLoggerOptions.cs changed from rejecting 0 to accepting it. `FileLoggerProvider` only prunes old files when `_maxRetainedFiles > 0`, so 0 now means no pruning at all.

The setter for `BackgroundQueueSize` in BatchingLoggerOptions.cs changed from accepting 0 to rejecting it. `BatchingLoggerProvider` passes this value into a BlockingCollection bound, so the change moves the failure earlier, to setter time, and the message is stale.

`ValidationOptions` now sets the out parameter to null before iterating resolvers. The result is identical on every path, so this is a readability-neutral reorder. The brace on the `TryGetValidatableParameterInfo` signature is the only formatting regression.

The remaining changes are XML-doc-only: summaries, `<value>`, `<remarks>`, and `<see langword>` edits across the Polly builder extensions, SqlServerCacheOptions, and the Validation interfaces and attributes.

findings.title: RetainedFileCountLimit now accepts 0, contradicting its docs and disabling log pruning
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/AzureFileLoggerOptions.cs`, the `RetainedFileCountLimit` setter (around line 53) was changed from `value <= 0` to `value < 0` in a doc-only PR. The XML summary says "strictly positive" and the exception message says "must be positive," but 0 is now accepted. In `FileLoggerProvider.cs` (around line 76) a value of 0 disables pruning, so logs accumulate on disk. Restore the original `value <= 0` check so the code matches the docs and message. Leave the doc comment as is. Optionally add a unit test in `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/test` that asserts setting 0 throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

findings.title: BackgroundQueueSize now rejects 0, but its exception message still says non-negative
findings.body:
The `BackgroundQueueSize` setter changed from `value < 0` to `value <= 0`. That change is a behavior change, and it is not mentioned in the PR description.

The exception message was not updated. It still says `"BackgroundQueueSize must be non-negative."` That text is false for 0, which is now rejected. The new XML doc also doesn't say that 0 is invalid. It only says "or null for no limit."

The value flows into `BatchingLoggerProvider`, where it becomes the bound of a `BlockingCollection` (around line 157). I believe a non-positive bound was already rejected there, so the practical effect is that the error is raised earlier, at setter time instead of provider start. Callers that set 0 in a try/catch around provider creation will see the failure move.

::diff{file="src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs" lines="42-54"}

Either revert the operator to keep the original timing, or keep the new check and change the message to "must be positive" and state the rule in the `<value>` block.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs`, the `BackgroundQueueSize` setter (around line 47) was changed to reject 0 (`value <= 0`), but the thrown message on line 49 still says "must be non-negative." Pick one: either revert to `value < 0` to preserve the original behavior, or keep `value <= 0` and change the message to "must be positive." If keeping the stricter check, also state in the `<value>` XML block that the value must be positive, and call out the behavior change in the PR description. Verify against `BatchingLoggerProvider.cs` around line 157, where the value becomes the BlockingCollection bound.

findings.title: Brace placement breaks the file's Allman style on TryGetValidatableParameterInfo
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Validation/src/ValidationOptions.cs`, the `TryGetValidatableParameterInfo` method signature (around line 66) has its opening brace on the same line as the signature. Move the `{` onto its own line to match the Allman style used by the other methods in this file and by the repo's `.editorconfig`. No logic change.

findings.title: Typo in PollyHttpClientBuilderExtensions summary: "extensions methods"
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/HttpClientFactory/Polly/src/DependencyInjection/PollyHttpClientBuilderExtensions.cs` line 14, the class summary says "Provides extensions methods for configuring..." Change "extensions methods" to "extension methods". Doc comment only.

findings.title: SqlServer ExpiredItemsDeletionInterval docs omit the enforced 5-minute minimum
findings.body:
The rewritten summary for `ExpiredItemsDeletionInterval` says the interval is used to scan and delete expired items and that the default is 30 minutes. It does not mention that `SqlServerCache` rejects any value below 5 minutes. The check is in the constructor at `src/Caching/SqlServer/src/SqlServerCache.cs` lines 44-49, and it throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

This PR is specifically a docs refresh for these options, so this is the moment to document the constraint. Without it, a user can set 1 minute and only find out at startup.

::diff{file="src/Caching/SqlServer/src/SqlServerCacheOptions.cs" lines="19-27"}

Add a sentence to the `<value>` block, for example: "The value cannot be less than 5 minutes."
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Caching/SqlServer/src/SqlServerCacheOptions.cs`, the `ExpiredItemsDeletionInterval` XML doc (around line 21, and the `<value>` block after it) does not say that values under 5 minutes are rejected. `SqlServerCache.cs` lines 44-49 enforce a `MinimumExpiredItemsDeletionInterval` of 5 minutes. Add one sentence to the `<value>` block stating the 5-minute minimum, and keep the existing 30-minute default text. Doc comment only.

findings.title: Doc rewrites are accurate and use the .NET doc conventions well
Moving the out-parameter reset to the top of ValidationOptions is behavior-preserving
findings.body:
In `TryGetValidatableTypeInfo`, `validatableTypeInfo = null` now runs before the resolver loop instead of after it. The return value and final out value are the same on every path, because the loop only assigns the out parameter and returns early on success. The reordering is harmless, and it makes the null-on-miss contract easier to read.

::diff{file="src/Validation/src/ValidationOptions.cs" lines="40-55"}
